name.title: DP_ECE_RT_STATS
name.sysdesc: A data product which reports operational statistics of the ECE remote terminal.

array.sysdesc: The state of every client service request slot maintained by rt_svc. This information describes the set of RT service requests currently requested (and not requested) of rt_svc by cstr_mgr.

field.sysdesc: 1553 service direction (either XMIT or RECV)
1553 service subaddress (0-31)
The size, in number of 16-bit data words, of the client request buffer
The number of 16-bit data words which have already been transferred over the 1553 bus for this service request
The overall success/failure status of the service request.
Boolean flag. 0 implies that this service request is opportunistic. 1 implies that this service request is critical.

array.sysdesc: This array reports the data words in the STM which was last received by the ECE RT.

field.sysdesc: One U16 word value. The index of the 1553 data word corresponds to the index within this DP array (e.g., index 0 is data word 0, index 1 is data word 1, etc.)
The number of 1553 words in the most recent STM received by the ECE RT
The current service state of rt_svc. Client requests cannot be serviced until rt_svc is in the READY state.
Boolean field indicating TRUE if a client is currently registered with rt_svc and FALSE otherwise.

This count indicates the number of 32hz cycles during which rt_svc was in the NOT_READY state during the most recent initialization. This gives an indication of how long it took to initialize the service. The 64-bit uint can report a maximum count of about 1553.45 days before rolling over.

This count indicates the number of 32hz cycles during which rt_svc was in the PROCESS_STM state during the most recent initialization. This gives an indication of how much time elapsed before time was established and rt_svc began servicing client requests. The 64-bit uint can report a maximum count of about 1553.45 days before rolling over.
This count indicates the number of bad STMs that have been received by the ECE RT.
